FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards/ after the 
draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 

Pen point is a drawing instrument accessory used by draughtsmen and engineers along with half 
set of compasses or handle for drawing straight lines and circles in ink. 

The standard was originally published in 1965. This revision is based on further experience gained 
in the manufacture of drawing instruments and ether developments in this field. 

In this standard the tolerances on important dimensions and mating parts have be^n specified. The 
dimensions of pen part fixing shanks have also been modified from 3 mm to 3*5 and 4 mm. The 
overall length of the pen part has been modified from 55 mm approximately to 57 ± 0*5 mm and 
an additional size of 41 ± 0'5 mm too has been included. 

In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 58511-1976 
'Prazision-Resszeuge (P ) Reessfederinsatze ( Pen part )', issued by the Deutsches Normenausschu 
B Zeichnungswesen ( NZ ) IM DIN, 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance 
with IS 2 : 1960 * Rules for rounding oflF numerical values ( revised )\ The number of significant 
places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 
standard. 



IS 3211 : 1991 



Indian Standard 



ENGINEERS' DRAWING INSTRUMENTS, 

PEN POINTS 



( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This Indian Standard covers the requirements of 
pen points for engineers' drawing instruments of 
following types: 

a) Pen pointy plain nib; 

b) Pen point, shifting nib; and 

c) Pen point, lifting nib.

3 MATERIAL AND HARDNESS 

3,1 The material for manufacture of pen points 
shall be steel having a carbon content of 0*60 
to 0'75 percent or a suitable grade of stainless 
steel. 



3.2 The nibs shall have a minimum 
of230HV. 

4 DIMENSIONS 



hardness 



The dimensions for pen points shall be as shown 
in Fig. 1. 

4.1 The tolerance on interchangeable dimensions 
shall be as shown in Fig. 1 and shall be capable 
of being locked tight with the locking screw. 

4.2 The figure is intended only to illustrate the 
dimensions and the design detail is left to the 
discretion of the manufacturer so long as the 
specified dimensions are maintained. 

5 DESIGNATION 

Pen points shall be designated by the commonly 
used name, diameter of fixing shank and number 
of this standard. 

Example : 

Pen points with shifting nib of shank dia 4 
complete with screws shall be designated as: 
Pen point. Shifting Nib of shank dia 4 IS 3211

6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

6.1 The drawing nibs for pen points shall have a 

well designed ink space between the two blades 
and their points rounded in an elliptical form for 
smooth working. 

6.2 The lifting nibs should be so constructed that 
it forms a spring in itself and shall remain tightly 
pressed against the adjusting screw throughout 
the range of its setting. 

6.3 The plain and shifting nibs should be rigid 
and be able to resist any movement caused by 
pressure necessary for using against the rigid 
edge. 

7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

7.1 When pen points are made from carbon steel, 
they shall be chromium plated to service Grade 
No. 2 according to IS 1068 : 1985. 

7.2 The drawing nibs shall be hardened, tempered, 
polished and honed. 

8 SCREWS 

The different screws used with pen points shall 
conform to the requirements as specified in 
IS 3222 ( Part 1 ) : 1989. 

9 TEST 

9.1 Dimensional Test 

The pen points shall be tested for conformity 
with the requirements of dimensions as specified 
in 4. 

9.2 Hardness Test 



10 SAMPLING 

10.1 Lot 

In a consignment all the pen points of the same 
type and size, manufactured from same material 
under similar conditions of production shall be 
grouped together to constiute a lot, 

10-2 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
supplier and the purchaser, the procedure given 
in IS 2500 ( Part 1) : 1973 shall be followed for 
sampling inspection. The inspection level, accep- 
table quality level ( AQL ) and type of sampling 
plan to be followed for various characteristics 
shall be as given in 10.2.1 and 10.2.2. 

10.2.1 For dimensions, designation, general 
requirements, workmanship and finish, a single 
sampling plan with inspection level IV and AQL 
of 2*5 percent as given in Tables 1 and 2 of 
IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1973 shall be followed. 

10.2.2 For screws 8 a single sampling plan with 
inspection levell 11 and AQL of 2'5 percent as 
given in Tables 1 and 2 of IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1973 
shall be followed. 

11 MARKING 

The pen points shall be marked with the source 
of manufacture or trade-mark at a suitable place. 

12 PACKING 



12.1 The pen points shall be first wrapped 
paper and then packed in a suitable carton. 



m

in 3.2. 



shall be tested for hardness specified 



12.2 The pen points may also be suppUed as a 
part of an instruments set in which case the com- 
plete set may be supplied in a suitable box. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a furthet safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Boreftu of Indimi Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country.

designations. Enquires relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS.
